verification_quality_findings.finding: Both tests pass with _escape_label reduced to the identity function (mutation M1, 104/104 still green). Their PASS does not depend on the behaviour they name - they pass because route_label() returns a bounded template, so the crafted path never reaches a label at all (confirmed: M3 is what kills these same tests). Escaping is the documented defence for AC2's 'no injected series' and is dead code from the suite's point of view. The escape table also omits CR and 29 other C0 characters, which is harmless only while every label value is drawn from a fixed set.
verification_quality_findings.suggestion: Unit-test _escape_label directly against backslash, double quote, \n, \r and a C0 sample. Do not test it through a request; the request path can no longer carry the payload to it.

verification_quality_findings.finding: The AC's premise ('an application payload ... when the request is served') cannot exist: no endpoint accepts a payload and the story's own Scope Out forbids adding one. The test satisfies the AC by calling redact_values() itself and asserting the values it just registered are absent, while the served request is GET /health carrying no PII. Zero register_sensitive/redact_values call sites exist in backend/src. ba457bf added the call sites to the spec Operations, not to code, so round 2's escalation trigger has not fired.
verification_quality_findings.suggestion: Record as a spec defect against E15-S1-AC1 rather than carrying it as a green criterion. Credit where due: the suite documents its own vacuity and ships a paired non-vacuity control that will bite when E4-S1 lands.

verification_quality_findings.finding: Circular: both walk the same logging.root.manager.loggerDict that _install_redaction_filter_everywhere had just walked. The non-vacuity probe logging.Logger('unregistered-probe-logger') is constructor-built so never enters loggerDict; it proves only that the predicate returns False for a bare object. Measured consequence: a logger created after configure_logging has no own filter (False) while the root handler still filters (True) - no leak, but 'installed on 100%' is time-of-configure scoped.
verification_quality_findings.suggestion: Register a real logger via logging.getLogger() AFTER configure_logging and assert the enumeration reports it, or state the property as 'the root handler filters every record' which is what actually holds.

verification_quality_findings.finding: Escapes 3 of 32 control-relevant characters; leaves \t, \r and 28 other C0 characters raw. Unreachable today. If reached, degrades the exposition to unparseable (prom-parse.js returns [], errorRate null, sensor warn) rather than forgeable, because the quote escape holds.
verification_quality_findings.suggestion: Escape or strip all C0 characters, not just \n.

verification_quality_findings.finding: Asserts only on client.get('/metrics').text; never checks the response is text/plain.
